turns.t: G'day, doctor. I'll be honest, I'm a bit freaked out. My wife filmed me sleeping and I stop breathing.
That would worry anyone. Tell me what the video showed.
I snore like a chainsaw, and then it goes quiet for, I don't know, ten seconds, then I make this awful snorting gasp. Over and over.
How long has the snoring been going on?
Years, but the pauses are new, she only noticed this month.
Do you wake up tired?
Wrecked. I'm dozing at traffic lights. That's what really scares me.
Any morning headaches, or a dry mouth when you wake?
No headaches, no. Dry mouth, yeah, a bit, but no headaches.
Do you ever wake up choking or gasping?
No, I don't think I wake up. She says I just gasp and carry on.
Is your nose blocked at night?
Always. Both sides. I breathe through my mouth.
Any allergies, to medicines especially?
Oh, something gave me a swollen lip once, years ago, but I don't know what it was. A tablet, I think. Or maybe food.
So possibly an allergic reaction, but you can't say what to. I'll note it as uncertain. Do you drink in the evenings?
A couple of beers, most nights. I know, I know.
That relaxes the throat muscles and makes snoring worse. Let me look at your nose and throat. Say ahh. ~
Ahhh.
Your nostrils are swollen inside, and the throat's crowded at the back. That's why you're snoring. ~
Is it sleep apnoea, then? ~
What you describe, loud snoring, pauses in breathing, and daytime sleepiness, looks most like obstructive sleep apnoea.
Right. Is that serious? ~
It can be, over time, and it's a real safety risk if you're drowsy driving. So I want to be definite about the next steps. ~
What do I do? ~
I'll refer you to the sleep clinic for a proper sleep study.
How long will that take? ~
A few weeks, I'm afraid. Meanwhile, I'd like to start you on a nasal spray, fluticasone, two sprays in each nostril once a day, to open your nose up.
Okay. Will that fix it? ~
It won't cure sleep apnoea, but it can help the snoring, and make any treatment easier. Give it a fortnight. ~
What about the driving? ~
Please don't drive when you feel drowsy, pull over and take a break. And cut the beer in the evenings.
Fair. ~
I'd like to see you again in three weeks, to see how the nose is and where the sleep clinic has got to.
Three weeks. Brilliant, thanks, doc. ~

chief_complaint.value: my wife filmed me sleeping and I stop breathing

clinical_actions.description: Refer to sleep clinic for a sleep study
Advise not driving when drowsy and cutting evening beer

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient recalls a swollen lip after something (a tablet or food) but cannot name the substance.

social_history.details: A couple of beers, most nights
